Check whether a block design satisfies CDCM identifiability assumptions

check_design_identifiability.Rd

Evaluates practical sufficient-condition diagnostics for the CDCM identifiability result under a block-design experimental input. The function checks whether the full scan contains enough usable blocks and whether the corresponding block-level stimulus combinations are sufficiently unconfounded.

Usage

check_design_identifiability(data, tol = 1e-08, warn = TRUE)

Arguments

data

A list containing:

  • times: a numeric vector of equally spaced observation times.

  • u: a \(T \times m\) numeric matrix encoding the stimulus inputs at each observation time.

  • y_obs: a \(T \times d\) numeric matrix of observed ROI-level BOLD signals.

tol

Numeric tolerance used for the equal-spacing and matrix-rank checks. Defaults to 1e-8.

warn

Logical; if TRUE, warnings are issued when one or more diagnostics are not satisfied. Defaults to TRUE.

Value

A list containing:

cond_A1

Logical indicating whether the A1 diagnostic is satisfied.

cond_A2

Logical indicating whether the A2 diagnostic is satisfied.

all_ok

Logical indicating whether both diagnostics are satisfied.

equally_spaced

Logical indicating whether the observation times are equally spaced up to tol.

n_eligible_blocks

Number of blocks containing at least \(d + 1\) observations.

rank_U_aug

Rank of the augmented block-level stimulus matrix formed from eligible blocks.

Details

This function checks the experimental design assumptions used in the CDCM identifiability result. The input matrix u is provided at the observation level, with each row corresponding to \(u(t_j)\). Since the design is assumed to be blockwise constant, the block-level stimulus vector \(\tilde u^{(b)}\) is obtained by taking the first row of u within each block.

Assumption (A1) is checked by verifying that the observation times are equally spaced and that at least \(m + 1\) blocks contain at least \(d + 1\) observations, where \(d\) is the number of ROIs and \(m\) is the number of stimulus inputs.

Assumption (A2) is checked by forming the augmented block-level stimulus matrix $$ U^* = \left[ \begin{array}{cc} 1 & \tilde{u}^{(b_1)T} \\ \vdots & \vdots \\ 1 & \tilde{u}^{(b_q)T} \end{array} \right] $$ from the blocks satisfying A1's block-length requirement, and checking whether this matrix has rank \(m + 1\). This is equivalent to checking whether there exists a subset of \(m + 1\) usable blocks whose augmented stimulus matrix is invertible.

These diagnostics are sufficient-condition checks. Failure to satisfy one or more diagnostics does not necessarily imply that the model is not identifiable, but it may indicate that the design is weak for reliable estimation.
